title: void Functions and Side Effects
learningObjectives: Describe void functions and observable side effects.
Identify output, mutation and early-return behavior.
Trace what each call changes or displays.
Keep side effects explicit and avoid unrelated actions.
Design a void helper with one clear responsibility.

understand.concept: A void function performs an action but does not return a value. It can print, update an object through a reference, or perform another side effect. A bare return exits a void function.
understand.whyItMatters: Action-oriented helpers can keep menus, reports, formatting and state-changing operations organized without inventing return values.
understand.explain: Choose void when the caller does not need a computed result. Keep side effects obvious and focused. Avoid hidden changes to global state, and use a reference parameter only when the function is intentionally modifying caller-owned data.

examples.title: Display a greeting
examples.explanation: The function prints and returns no value.

examples.title: Print a row of stars
examples.explanation: The caller supplies the desired width.

examples.title: Modify via reference
examples.code: void addTen(int& value){value+=10;}\nint score=5;addTen(score); // score becomes 15
examples.explanation: The reference parameter intentionally changes the caller's variable.

examples.title: Print a separator
examples.explanation: A small formatting helper avoids repeating the same output line.

examples.title: Exit early
examples.explanation: A bare return exits the function without returning a value.

practise.guidedTask: For void Functions and Side Effects, inspect each example and annotate the function signature, call site, argument values, local state, return or side-effect behavior. Compare the cases and explain why each design choice fits.
practise.independentTask: Write a short C++ program applying void Functions and Side Effects. Include at least three related functions/calls, then test typical inputs, boundary values, and one invalid or unusual case where applicable. Explain the expected result for each test.
hints: Start by stating the helper's contract and intended behavior.
Trace one call using concrete argument values.
Keep computation separate from display unless output is the function's purpose.
Check boundary values and any invalid-input path.
Review scope, return type and side effects before finalizing.

questions.prompt: Can a void function have side effects?
questions.explanation: It may output or update caller-owned state.
A bare return ends a void function.
Clear side effects are easier to reason about.
